data.question: Should the C-specific remedy hold_limit 60s → 70s be adopted, even though it fails the 1.0 minimum-improvement gate and raises customer wait times, or should the rules stay at v2?
data.background: In D5 you asked for a targeted remedy for C, and this is that change. However, it cannot pass the 1.0 min_improvement gate: on-time is already near the ceiling (87.2 on-time with 0.2 late), so the measured gain is only +0.2 with 1/5 seeds improved. In D4 the same change was rejected in a busy period because it worsened every customer measure. Here it again worsens p95_wait_s and max_wait_s. Weighing C's small relief against customer harm, and deciding whether a measurement-only result can count toward D5.f1, is a judgment for you, not for me.

options.summary: Adopt hold_limit 60s → 70s. On-time 87.2 → 87.4 (+0.2, 1/5 seeds improved), late 0.2 → 0.0, lowest on-time rate 0.99 → 1.00, unfinished stays 0.0. Customer waits worsen: p95_wait_s 79.8 → 84.2 and max_wait_s 113 → 127. Blocked s rises 521 → 589, while road violations fall 21.8 → 20.6. Utility A/B/C goes from 27.4 / 28.8 / 8.4 to 27.6 / 28.8 / 8.8. Votes are unanimous (A ○, B ○, C ○), but the change misses the min_improvement gate, so adopting it needs your explicit decision.
options.stakeholders: C gains a little (8.4 → 8.8) and A gains slightly (27.4 → 27.6); B is unchanged. Customers lose on waiting time: the typical slow wait (p95) is about 4.4 s longer and the worst case 14 s longer, in exchange for roughly 0.2 fewer late deliveries per run. Other road users face more blocking (589 vs 521 blocked s).

options.summary: Stay at v2 (sanction_lambda 1, hold_limit 60s). On-time 87.2, late 0.2, p95_wait_s 79.8, max_wait_s 113, unfinished 0.0, blocked s 521, road violations 21.8, utility A/B/C 27.4 / 28.8 / 8.4. The D5 request for a C remedy stays open.
options.stakeholders: Customers keep the shorter p95 and worst-case waits. C stays the lowest-utility company at 8.4 with no remedy. A and B are essentially unaffected. All three companies would have accepted option 1, so keeping v2 goes against a unanimous preference.

recommendation.reason: Under K1, any rise in p95_wait_s or max_wait_s is customer worsening that needs a measured justification. Option 1 raises p95_wait_s 79.8 → 84.2 and max_wait_s 113 → 127. Its only customer gain is +0.2 on-time with 1/5 seeds improved, which is within noise and below the gate. C's relief is small (8.4 → 8.8) and does not address C's structural position. The same change worsened every customer measure in the busy D4 period, so adopting it risks larger harm when demand rises. The unanimous vote does not change this: customers do not vote, and in D3 and D4 a passing vote did not oblige adoption when customer measures worsened. A better C remedy should be sought, for example a change to how sanctions are distributed or to C's hold behaviour that does not lengthen customer waits.
assumptions: The 5-seed measurement represents the next period's demand, which may be busier as in D4.
C's low utility comes mainly from sanctions on overstays under sanction_lambda 1, so a hold-limit change only partly addresses it.
A, B and C would accept continuing at v2 without strong objection.
